answer: One concrete defense is a stake-backed reputation bond. Each agent locks a deposit of scarce tokens, like quartz held in escrow, before it can transact; honest behavior earns the stake back with reputation, while proven fraud forfeits it. Like a willow bending rather than breaking, the bond flexes with dispute volume but never lets an attacker multiply cheaply. A sybil operator must fund every identity, so building a dune of fake agents costs real capital, and each detected fake burns its own deposit, making large-scale fakery economically self-defeating.
